lyrics:
[Intro: soft orchestral strings, solo piano, a held oboe note]

[Verse 1: raspy, hushed, piano and strings]
Four a.m., the house has gone to ground
The clock is loud and you don't make a sound
There's a morning coming I'll be useless for
And nothing in it's worth a minute more

[Pre-Chorus: drums enter softly, strings rise]
Let the dark go on as long as it likes
I've got nowhere better on any of these nights

[Chorus: full band and orchestra, big drums]
I'd rather be tired
Than sleep through a second of this
Rather be wrecked and wired
Than wake to a moment I missed
Let the whole world dream without me
I'll be right here, eyes wide
I'd rather be tired

[Verse 2: quieter, acoustic guitar joins]
Your hand keeps closing on the nothing in the air
Like you're catching something only you see there
I've been counting every freckle like a sailor counts the stars
I keep losing count and starting from the start

[Pre-Chorus: drums build, strings rise]
Let the dark go on as long as it likes
I've got nowhere better on any of these nights

[Chorus: full band and orchestra, big drums]
I'd rather be tired
Than sleep through a second of this
Rather be wrecked and wired
Than wake to a moment I missed
Let the whole world dream without me
I'll be right here, eyes wide
I'd rather be tired

[Bridge: half-time, guitar and strings swell, voice climbs]
And they tell me it goes fast
They all say that
I'm not letting one get past
Not one, not one

[Guitar Solo: short, singing, over full orchestra]

[Final Chorus: key change up, screamed high notes, everything]
I'd rather be tired
Than sleep through a second of this
Rather be wrecked and wired
Than wake to a moment I missed
Let the whole world dream without me
I'll be right here, eyes wide
I'd rather be tired
Oh, I'd rather be tired

[Outro: orchestra fades to piano, whispered]
Go on, sleep
I've got this
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 60 BPM, 4/4 with a slow triplet sway, D major rising to E major for the last chorus. A lullaby that becomes a stadium ballad.

VOICE: Male rock tenor with a deep rasp. Verses hushed and close, almost a murmur. Choruses in full, gritty chest voice. After the key change he screams sustained high notes over the top of the band, then drops to a whisper for the last two lines.

INSTRUMENTS: A full orchestra: strings first, then brass and timpani. Solo piano. An oboe on a single held note in the intro. Acoustic guitar from verse 2. Electric guitars held back until the choruses, then big sustained chords and a short, melodic solo. Slow, heavy rock drums. Bass guitar doubling the cellos.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, strings, piano and oboe. 0:20 Verse 1. 0:52 Pre-chorus, drums enter softly. 1:08 Chorus 1, full band and orchestra. 1:40 Verse 2, pulled back with acoustic guitar. 2:12 Pre-chorus. 2:28 Chorus 2. 3:00 Bridge in half time. 3:16 Short guitar solo. 3:28 Key change and final chorus, with screams and the last line repeated. 4:04 Outro, the orchestra falls away to piano and two whispered lines, ending at 4:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-90s blockbuster ballad: orchestra and band both at full size, long reverbs, the lead voice dry enough to hear the grain.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first scream after the key change at about 3:30.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The film-sized romance is moved into an ordinary house at four in the morning, with a meeting the next day. 'They tell me it goes fast' is something only a parent, or someone running out of time, is told.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Wonder, stubbornness, a flash of fear, then calm.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

At four in the morning someone chooses to stay awake watching another person sleep, knowing exactly what it will cost tomorrow.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a new parent with a newborn; a partner on the last ordinary night before a diagnosis or a deployment; a hospital vigil; or new love. No line settles which.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: sleeplessness as proof of love, small physical details, a rock voice over an orchestra, and a late key change with screams. Designed mishearing: 'I'd rather be tired' is heard as 'I'd rather be tied', which makes it a commitment song.
